doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Art Ensemble of Chicago and avant-garde
summary: He praises the Art Ensemble and says avant-garde works when players can play straight ahead.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Ok. I see you also booked the Art Ensemble of Chicago.

Yeah, I dug them. They had some humor about them and some... Lester Bowie has a humor about him. He wasn’t all “oh boy, this is,” you know. And they could play. Don Moye was a marvelous percussionist. And I had heard avant-garde before that; the ACM wasn’t the first ones. Joe Daly and Hal Russell had stuff going way before that. And it was ok, but they came from the straight-ahead stuff, and that’s the kind of avant-garde I like. It was played by people who know how to play straight ahead, because I feel to have freedom, you have to be free from something. You can’t just pick up a horn and go “blblblblbl” which is what a lot of them are doing.
